transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Tara Singh (StratusWave Head Partnerships), Liam O'Connor (StratusWave Global Sales), Priya Rao (StratusWave Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Quick run through of the top three joint accounts (Atlas, Meridian, & Luma)
- Identified Atlas as highest near-term close; need technical bench test vs EdgeServe latency claims
- Security: SOC2 attestation requested, encryption at-rest key mgmt question, VPC peering callout
- Next steps agreed: joint quote, technical demo, security artifact exchange

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um I think we said 30 minutes but we had a few extra so we'll go 45ish, is that okay?
[00:08] Tara Singh: That's fine, we blocked an hour so we're good.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Quick intro from our side, Marcus here, I'm the solutions engineer, I run the latency and perf work for redwood — uh Redwood Dedicated and Private.
[00:21] Liam O'Connor: Liam from StratusWave sales, nice to meet you Marcus.
[00:24] Priya Rao: Priya here, I'll be handling security gating and compliance questions, quick heads up we have a FedRAMP-ish customer in the mix so timing is sensitive.
[00:33] Avery Chen: Great. High level: goal for today is to handoff the top pipeline, surface any blockers, and agree next steps for Atlas. Tara, can you give a 2 minute cadence on how StratusWave prioritizes partner-sourced deals?
[00:45] Tara Singh: Sure, so typically deals with ARR > $250K we route through the partner desk, Atlas is a 500K ARR potential, they have a multi-region footprint so data residency is a big checkbox. We've done the initial exec intro, they asked for benchmark vs EdgeServe on throughput and cold-start latency.
[01:05] Avery Chen: Good, that aligns with what we saw. Marcus, quick take on the Atlas technical ask?
[01:10] Marcus Lee: Right, they want steady-state throughput at 2k tokens/sec at p99 < 350ms for short chat flows, and they care about burst isolation. We can do that on Dedicated or Private, but note Dedicated gives better multi-tenant accounting and burst pools. Also, the customer asked about prefix caching — that's something we can enable to reduce cost.
[01:34] Liam O'Connor: When you say Dedicated vs Private — what's the typical delta on TCO? They quoted NimbusAI as cheaper in their eval.
[01:42] Marcus Lee: Short answer: Dedicated is mid-range cost but highest predictability; Private (VPC/on-prem) has higher ops and setup cost but better isolation. In many cases Redwood can tune quantization profiles to match cost parity with Nimbus for specific workloads; will need actual token distributions.
[02:00] Tara Singh: On the commerce side we need partner margin tiers, like what discount we can pass to ATLAS and what our MDF looks like. Avery?
[02:09] Avery Chen: We're preparing a partner discount schedule — I'll include a scenario table: co-sell split, MDF credit, and renewal uplift threshold. I can share a draft by Monday.
[02:20] Priya Rao: Security — I have several quick items: do you have SOC2 and ISO artifacts, what's your encryption at rest model, and do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? Also data retention: can you delete customer tokens on request?
[02:36] Marcus Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs — I'll send links. For encryption, we support AES-256 at rest; for Private we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Token deletion is supported via retention APIs, though the terminology sometimes surfaces as "KV cash" in notes, but it's KV cache / prefix TTLs; we'll clarify.
[02:58] Priya Rao: Cool, please include sample logs and audit trail retention windows.
[03:03] Avery Chen: Noted. We'll put security pack in the shared folder. Link: https://redwood.app/partner-dealpack/CRM-45821 (shortlink, will share full later).
[03:15] Tara Singh: Great. On timeline, Atlas wants a pilot in 6 weeks. Is that realistic?
[03:20] Marcus Lee: For a minimal pilot, yes — hosted Redwood API with a dedicated pool can be stood up quickly, 2-3 weeks for config and test, plus 1-2 weeks for integration testing at customer side. Private deployment adds 4-6 extra weeks because of VPC and KMS setup.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: They flagged regulatory folks — our fight is to avoid Private if possible due to cloud ops overhead.
[03:41] Avery Chen: Understood; we'll aim for Dedicated first and have Private as fallback.
[03:46] Tara Singh: There's also Meridian, a lower ARR but fast close — do we want to prioritize Atlas over Meridian?
[03:52] Marcus Lee: Atlas has higher strategic value and large seat counts, Meridian might be good for quick reference but won't move the needle on revenue as much. Recommend prioritizing Atlas as primary.
[04:03] Tara Singh: Ok we'll do that.
[04:06] Liam O'Connor: Competitor noise — Atlas mentioned a sales deck from EdgeServe claiming 40% lower latency at p50 using their custom kernel. Are we willing to run a head-to-head?
[04:17] Marcus Lee: Yes we can do a head-to-head. We'll run a baseline with their reported sequence length distribution. Note: benchmarks often differ in prompt design so we should get Atlas to share sample prompts. I'll parameterize the run and share a spreadsheet with runs.
[04:33] Tara Singh: Action item: Atlas to share sample prompt set. I'll ask them after this call.
[04:38] Priya Rao: Also, legal — we need to know if Redwood supports contract terms like data residency addendum and limited sub-processing.
[04:46] Avery Chen: We have boilerplate addenda we can share. I'll ask legal to prepare a partner-friendly addendum and send it over.
[04:54] Liam O'Connor: For sales plays, StratusWave wants co-branded case study language and a joint exec briefing pack.
[05:00] Avery Chen: We can do that; we'll assign a field marketing contact after this handoff.
[05:05] Tara Singh: On margin, what's the partner-friendly discount band?
[05:09] Avery Chen: Typical band for strategic partners is 15–25% depending on commit. For Atlas-sized deals we can increase to 30% with MDF and co-sell credit. I'll include a 3-tier with thresholds in the deck.
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: Cool.
[05:23] (short pause / shuffling)
[05:27] Marcus Lee: Quick technical clarification: Atlas asked about KV cache and prompt routing across regions — we support prefix caching and region-based routing; however, cache warmup times vary. If they want consistent p99 across regions, Private is easier but Dedicated with multi-region routing works too.
[05:48] Priya Rao: Will you provide detailed network diagram for Dedicated + VPC peering? Our infra team will need it.
[05:54] Marcus Lee: Yes, I'll draw up a simplified network diagram and include sample ip ranges, firewall rules, and peering notes.
[06:01] Tara Singh: Any red flags we should know about ahead of sending to Atlas?
[06:04] Avery Chen: One thing — model version pinning: be explicit on model versions and fallback plans. If Atlas requires strict determinism we'll need to agree on pinned version and rollout policy. Also, tokenization differences can affect cost estimates, so we'll add token estimates per prompt.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: On procurement, Atlas wants payment terms net 60 — is that negotiable?
[06:25] Avery Chen: Standard is net 30, but for enterprise we can do net 45 with finance approval; net 60 may require a purchase order & legal signoff. I'll flag with finance.
[06:34] (crosstalk)
[06:36] Tara Singh: Okay great. Let's confirm next steps so nothing falls through.
[06:40] Avery Chen: I propose these next steps: 1) Avery sends partner discount schedule and draft quote by 2026-09-13, 2) Marcus runs perf baseline and shares spreadsheet by 2026-09-16, 3) Redwood sends SOC 2/ISO links + security pack by 2026-09-10, 4) StratusWave to get sample prompts and legal flags from Atlas by 2026-09-11. Does that sound right?
[07:01] Tara Singh: Yes that aligns.
[07:03] Priya Rao: I'll prioritize the security doc exchange.
[07:06] Marcus Lee: For the perf baseline I'll need a small instance of their prompt set and expected QPS. If they can't provide that, we'll approximate with similar seq lengths.
[07:16] Liam O'Connor: I'll coordinate with Atlas for sample prompts and push for the pilot timeline.
[07:20] Avery Chen: Perfect. Any final questions?
[07:23] Tara Singh: One more — how do we handle joint account ownership in your CRM? We want to make sure pipeline crediting is clear.
[07:29] Avery Chen: We typically do 50/50 credit for co-sell unless one party brings the majority of the technical validation. We can codify that in a SOW. I'll add a CRM note: "co-sell split: 50/50 pending SOW".
[07:42] Liam O'Connor: Sounds fair.
[07:44] (brief silence)
[07:46] Priya Rao: Also, audit logs — retention length please.
[07:49] Marcus Lee: Default logs 90 days in hosted; enterprise add-ons extend to 2 years. We'll include retention table in the security pack.
[07:58] Tara Singh: Great, thanks everyone.
[08:01] Avery Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up via the shared drive and schedule the technical demo for the week of 2026-09-15. I'll send a calendar invite after this call.
[08:11] Liam O'Connor: Appreciate it.
[08:13] Marcus Lee: Thanks all — talk soon.
[08:15] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings around KV cache (sometimes "K-V cash") and vendor names; timestamps approximate.

- Marcus: Run throughput/latency baseline vs EdgeServe and share spreadsheet (due 2026-09-16)
- Marcus: Network diagram + firewall rules for Dedicated/VPC (due 2026-09-10)
- Redwood Legal/Avery: Share partner-friendly addendum and SOC2/ISO links (due 2026-09-10)

End of transcript.
